Resolves #4665

Delayed VDOM collection, canvas polling, window observations, hidden rendering and iframe-focus forwarding now retire with their owning instance. Ten native delay sites use `core.Base#timeout`; that primitive also refuses a new wait after destruction. Canvas rejects late context acquisition at its entry point. Delays and next-task ordering remain intact.

Change class: restoration.
Evidence: L2 (local browser DOM/App-worker journeys plus isolated lifecycle controls) → L2 required; no installed-platform claim or deferred acceptance.

## AC Evidence
No structured ACs on #4665. The [source-grounded intake contract](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/4665#issuecomment-6666620210) resolves the old blanket prescription into ownership boundaries.

| Intake surface | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Destroyed Base allocates no wait | `BaseTimeout.spec.mjs`: no timer/registration after destruction; pre-aborted signal reason retained. |
| VDOM retirement before collection | `VdomDestroyCancellation.spec.mjs`: no batch after destruction during the 1ms yield; existing co-root cases retained. |
| Canvas retirement | `ContextAcquisition.spec.mjs`: pending poll cleared, retired callback cannot restart it, no later context acquisition. |
| Disconnect/reap ordering | `DepartedWindowReap.spec.mjs`; real popup-close journeys return panes without wedged updates. |
| Main observations/render scheduling | Native-route, move and render-queue tests retain observed-result/generation checks and both race winners. |
| Iframe focus forwarding | `DomEvents.spec.mjs`: next-task activeElement sample, no forwarding after retirement; six iframe/dock-rail browser cases. |
| Quiet dock projection retirement | `DockWorkspace.spec.mjs`: refresh and repair stand down before/during the owned delay; ordinary refresh errors still reject. |
| Close follow-up ownership | `DockHeaderActions.spec.mjs`: a settled close cannot focus a retired workspace/plugin. |
| Remote cancellation settlement | `ReplyLoss.spec.mjs`: destruction becomes a cloneable Error and removes the live caller's pending reply. |

## Deltas from ticket
The old “all occurrences” wording is not a mechanical replacement rule: native numeric-ID cancellation/rAF races, standalone utilities and the primitive's timer remain. `Main.closeTopologyWindow` retains its accepted terminal realm-close effect; route-token TTL cleanup retains its independent expiry. Canvas re-init/supersession is outside this destruction boundary.

Native-window test callbacks now defer instead of invoking synchronously before returning a timer ID. The render-queue harness drains task-created Promise continuations. Dock projection deferrals handle only their expected owner-retirement sentinel; close follow-ups recheck ownership before focusing chrome. The RMA rejection boundary converts that private Symbol into the existing Error reply shape so a live caller settles. Test cleanup no longer asks destroyed fixtures to own a new wait. [The experiment record](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/4665#issuecomment-6666920462) preserves the failed assumptions and evidence.

## Test Evidence
Zero-retry local browser checks: six `DockRailRevealIframe` component cases, the dedicated-worker painting case in `CanvasGroupPainting`, and both pane-return cases in `WorkstationPopupTargetCloseNL`. Explicit configs and isolated server/Bridge ports were used.

Before the fix, a destroyed Base still scheduled and resolved a timeout; a destroyed Canvas renderer's old callback scheduled another poll. New controls reject both outcomes. Focused lifecycle coverage passes. `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; syntax, whitespace, size checks and commit/push hooks cover their available gates.

A native MessageChannel probe also reproduced the old RMA clone failure and pending caller, then verified one ordinary Error reply and settled caller after the boundary repair. The full locked-dependency Engine unit run completed with no failed or flaky cases; its covered tests remain CI-owned evidence.

## Post-Merge Validation
None required for this instance-lifetime contract.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** Ticket #4665 (including our earlier #15000 premise read `IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABjLYbAw`, peer-role source audit `IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABjVhtpw`, and Sophie's intake contract `IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABjVyNMg` + experiment receipts `IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABjWEiDg` / `IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABjWWT7w` / `IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABjWt4bw`), changed-file list (21 files), and current `dev` source of `src/core/Base.mjs`, `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs`, `src/worker/App.mjs`, `src/canvas/Base.mjs`, `src/Main.mjs`, `src/main/DomEvents.mjs`, `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, `src/dashboard/dock/projection/Cycle.mjs`, `src/dashboard/dock/plugin/HeaderActions.mjs`, and `src/worker/mixin/RemoteMethodAccess.mjs`.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** `core.Base#timeout(time, {signal}={})` should reject immediately with `Neo.isDestroyed` without allocating or registering a timer when `me.isDestroyed` is already `true` (after checking a pre-aborted `signal`); instance-owned delays across `VdomLifecycle`, `worker.App`, `canvas.Base`, `Main` (focus/move/resize/close observations + hidden render drain), and `DomEvents#onWindowBlur` should migrate to `me.timeout(...)` while preserving numeric-ID cancellable/debounce/rAF timers, terminal `Main.closeTopologyWindow` realm-close authority, and independent route-token TTL cleanup; downstream consumers that await or chain those owned delays (dock projection refresh/repair, `HeaderActions` close focus, and `RemoteMethodAccess#reject` across `MessageChannel`/`postMessage`) must handle `Neo.isDestroyed` without `DataCloneError` or post-retirement focus.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches and improves the expected shape — in addition to the 10 owner-bound delay sites and the pre-destroyed entry guard in `src/core/Base.mjs:1215-1218` (plus entry guard in `src/canvas/Base.mjs:337`), the patch cleanly handles the three consumer boundaries surfaced by the full unit suite and cross-realm transport: (1) `projection/Cycle.mjs:92` and `Workspace.mjs:2915` swallow only `Neo.isDestroyed` on the 0ms deferral while rethrowing real refresh errors, (2) `HeaderActions.mjs:126` guards `(!me.isDestroyed && !this.isDestroyed && this.owner === me)` before post-close focus, and (3) `RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:304-306` converts `data === Neo.isDestroyed` into `new Error('Remote method target was destroyed')` so `structuredClone` does not throw `DataCloneError` and leave the remote caller pending.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert and friction→gold: rather than mechanically replacing all 49 `setTimeout` call sites (which would break numeric-ID `clearTimeout` debounce/rAF loops and terminal window close), Sophie falsified each lifetime class against live runtime and transport boundaries and fixed the real post-destruction timer and RMA serialization defects.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: None.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: None.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: `Neo.isDestroyed` is a private `Symbol('isDestroyed')`; when an async method on a remote target (such as `Neo.Main` window-observation polling via `this.timeout(50)`) rejects with `Neo.isDestroyed`, passing that raw Symbol to `postMessage` / `MessageChannel` in `RemoteMethodAccess#reject` throws a `DataCloneError` and strands the caller's pending promise forever. Translating `data === Neo.isDestroyed` to a cloneable `Error('Remote method target was destroyed')` at `RemoteMethodAccess#reject` preserves local Symbol semantics while guaranteeing cross-realm settlement.
